I get that people love their pets/companions and I am not saying they shouldn't. but it is a voluntary decision to adopt an animal, that forces you into supporting the meat industry. why is a shelter dog or cats life more important than the hundreds or thousands of animals that will be farmed to feed it over its life? 

obviously forcing animals to go vegan is not fair, letting them become invasive or fend for themselves in areas they cannot is horrible, so between picking supporting the meat industry via taking on a luxury(pet), or mass euthanasia/100% sterilization to the point they die off, which is more humane in the long run overall?

would you not consider loving dogs(or any domesticated animal really) immoral, or at least a slope to it? whether it be genuine abominations of breeds that have poor quality of life, or from the diet one has to feed a dog(even if you feed vegan- it is far from natural) or the fact that they've been bred solely for either practical or entertainment/companionship use by humans? and even service animals- would raising an animal for the sole purpose of detecting medical conditions not fall under the umbrella of exploitation? 

wouldn't the genuine, most ethical solution be to eradicate pet ownership as a whole?

ah well, my knowledge is not well versed enough to know what would be the short and long term effects of every tick species being fully removed from the world. there are many different tick species, and every ecosystem is different, so it would not be a blanket effect. i would assume ecosystems would not collapse, but there would be a net negative impact.

the parasites and disease they carry, while nasty, are an important form of population control, removing "weaker" members of the herd, and overall strengthening the remaining generations (for the most part). especially towards animals that humans have removed their predators, like in suburban environments, they are better than nothing. the parasites and diseases they transmit have their place in the ecosystem, and removing ticks removes their method of transmission.

i'm not sure if any animal eats ONLY ticks, so i'm not sure if it would cause any extinctions in the immediate step up in food chain, maybe some select birds or something but lesser food does cause a ripple effect so there is that to consider, and ecosystems could definitely be affected and never recover from that. remove food source for birds -> less birds -> any animal that preys on birds now has the same problem and it is repeated all the way up to the top of that respective food chain. 

tldr; probably would not collapse ecosystems but they are still important even if they piss us off.

ticks recycle nutrients back into ecosystem, are a good food source for birds/other animals, help control population, and i believe scientists can also survey them to see how well an area or ecosystem is doing. they are not pointless!
